## [2026-06-08T13:11:31Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

The user's formula needs clarification.

The formula likely uses the arithmetic mean of both factions' QNM strengths as a base value. The larger side would then receive a small growth bonus calculated as (their QNM / mean - 1) multiplied by 5%.

The larger side receives a 5% growth bonus relative to the arithmetic mean. The smaller side suffers a proportional slowdown. Progress is then divided by the LE-to-crime ratio, so stronger law enforcement slows down the raid timer.

Progress is divided by the LE-to-crime ratio. A higher law enforcement presence relative to crime slows the timer. This may apply citywide or to the target district.

Syndicate-versus-corporation wars multiply progress by 1.6. The larger side then uses a 25% bonus instead of 5%.

Each active war pair maintains two independent progress trackers.

Progress resets to zero when the war ends. At 50 percent the faction attacks the district with the most housing; ties favor lower district numbers. At 100 percent it attacks the district with the fewest assets; ties favor higher district numbers. Progress is then reduced by 100 percent. A target with only housing will trigger the housing raid at 50 percent and continue climbing toward 100 percent. A target with only assets will never reach the housing threshold, so it waits until 100 percent to trigger the asset raid.

The 50 percent housing raid triggers once when progress crosses that threshold. Progress does not reset at 50 percent. The 100 percent asset raid triggers once when progress crosses that threshold. Progress then drops by 100 percent.

Replaces the display-only stub in `Q.syncDistrictDisplays()` and wires into `monthly_tick_phase1`.\n\n**Roadmap:** [`roadmap.md`](../../roadmap.md) — District crime (planned).\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nCrime and collateral damage from warfare flow through **paramilitary groups** — armed capacity tied to a patron (or to nobody). Each month, sum **law-enforcement strength** and **outlaw strength** per district, form a **dominance ratio** `R`, and apply **threshold bands** (no continuous curve). Narrative events (blind eye, raid heat, …) apply **sudden out-of-band shocks** rather than slowly rewriting background levels.\n\n**Terminology:**\n\n| Term | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| **QNM** | **Q**uality, **N**umbers, **M**orale — the three stats that multiply into faction strength |\n| **LE** | Law-enforcement strength in a district (public order side) |\n| **Outlaw mass** | Criminal strength (syndicates + punks) |\n| **`R`** | `outlaw_mass / LE` — dominance ratio |\n| **District crime** | Output label (1–10, [`crime.qdisplay.dry`](../../qdisplays/crime.qdisplay.dry)) derived from `R` bands |\n| **Watch** | Background LE from district prosperity (flip side of punks) |\n\n---\n\n## QNM\n\nEach paramilitary has **quality**, **numbers**, **morale**, and **loyalty**.\n\n- **Strength** = `Q × N × M`\n- **Loyalty** caps how high morale can rise (rebellion phase later; already matters for police vs militia).\n\n**Starting posture:** city police — higher quality, **lower loyalty** (brittle, corruptible). Militias — lower quality, **more room to grow** via morale under sustained crime.\n\n---\n\n## Actors\n\n| Paramilitary | Patron | Role |\n|--------------|--------|------|\n| Syndicate muscle | Families, Edges, Sharks | District footprint; `prosperity_*` feeds QNM strength and (separately) drone bribery |\n| Corporate police | Soylent, Magrail, Brazos | Protect corp assets in home (and spill) districts |\n| City police | City government | Baseline public order; reform/defund changes QNM and loyalty |\n| Community militias | Democratic movement | Volunteer LE; lower starting quality, higher loyalty headroom |\n| Punks (name TBD) | None | Background outlaw strength when big players are quiet |\n| Watch | None (ambient) | Background LE from affluence / prosperity |\n\n**Rank dynamics:** syndicates and corps **do not** grow or shrink from the **LE balance** (dominance vs police/militia does not recruit or bleed ranks). Syndicate `prosperity_*` and future asset investment may expand ranks; corps hire from institutional budgets. Law enforcement does not face an ever-moving criminal headcount — only punks (and narrative shocks) drift on ambient conditions.\n\n**Exception:** syndicate **vs** syndicate war (open conflict) can cost **both** sides numbers and/or morale each month — the main way syndicate paramilitaries shrink outside narrative events.\n\n---\n\n## Building LE and outlaw mass\n\n### Public LE (per district)\n\n```\nLE = city_police + militia + watch + parochialism_nudge [+ corp_police_buff]\n```\n\n| Component | Source |\n|-----------|--------|\n| City police, militia | QNM strength in district |\n| **Watch** | Small bonus from population-weighted **district prosperity** |\n| Parochialism nudge | Very small LE boost from `Q.parochialism` (less than watch) |\n| Corp police buff | If leverage > reprisal: add `(3% × leverage) − (1% × reprisal)` of local corporate police strength (tune constants) |\n\n### Outlaw mass (per district)\n\n```\noutlaw_mass = sum(syndicate QNM in district) + punks\n```\n\nSyndicate `prosperity_*` and district G footprint feed syndicate QNM as **slow institutional inputs** (not monthly growth from beating LE). Mirror home-district links in [`PROSPERITY_IG_HOME_DISTRICT_LINKS`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry) (Families → Pitts + spill, Sharks → Deeps, etc.).\n\n### Dominance ratio\n\n```\nR = outlaw_mass / LE     (if LE <= 0, treat as collapsing)\n```\n\nSame ratio pattern reused for sub-matchups (corp assets, per-syndicate coercion) with their own thresholds where needed.\n\n---\n\n## Threshold bands\n\nDefault bands on **`R`** for public order. Dead zones between bands reduce monthly oscillation. Optional **hysteresis** (different cutoffs up vs down) if playtests show flip-flopping.\n\n### LE morale drift (police + militia)\n\nCompare **local** `R` with a **small citywide** spillover on the same bands.\n\n| Condition | Band | Effect |\n|-----------|------|--------|\n| `R < 0.20` | Secure | LE morale **rises** |\n| `0.20 ≤ R < 0.50` | Uneasy | Morale **steady** |\n| `0.50 ≤ R < 0.70` | Contested | LE morale **falls** |\n| `R ≥ 0.70` | Collapsing | Morale **falls** harder; civil-order-collapse effects |\n\nMilitia may use the same thresholds with faster step sizes. Low militia morale → [`militia_degrade.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/militia_degrade.scene.dry). [`security.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry) changes police QNM and loyalty.\n\n### Punks\n\nMorale/numbers drift **with** lawlessness (`R`), not from institutional budget.\n\n### District crime level (output)\n\nMap local `R` to `<district>_crime` (then blend city spillover below). Illustrative:\n\n| R | Crime band |\n|---|------------|\n| < 0.25 | Low |\n| 0.25 – 0.50 | Moderate |\n| 0.50 – 0.75 | High |\n| ≥ 0.75 | Severe |\n\nPlus `<district>_crime_modifier` stacks and minus `crime_relief_*` from [`community_outreach.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry).\n\n### City spillover\n\nEach district's **effective crime** ≈ **80% local + 20% city aggregate** (local control dominates).\n\n**City crime** = population-weighted average of district crime → `Q.crime_level`. Feeds tourism/longshore in [`organize_phase_tick.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry), [`PROSPERITY_PITTS_CRIME`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry), and citywide attitudes.\n\n### Other matchups (same ratio idea)\n\n| Matchup | Effect |\n|---------|--------|\n| Corp police vs local outlaw mass | Corp prosperity/affluence protected when corp dominates; narrowing gap reduces yield |\n| Each syndicate vs LE (+ enemy syndicate if at war) | Street coercion → district G shift; **not** rank growth |\n| Syndicate at war | Enemy strength added to LE **for that syndicate's coercion matchup only** (not general crime) |\n\n---\n\n## Open conflict\n\nWhen two paramilitaries are in **open conflict** (syndicate vs syndicate; corp vs corp while `cable_break_peace = 0`; syndicate vs corp):\n\n- Arithmetic **mean** of their QNM strengths → severity of violence, collateral damage, mutual attrition.\n- **Syndicate wars:** both sides lose numbers and/or morale proportional to intensity.\n- Corp wars: attrition TBD (morale/numbers and/or infra).\n- Collateral may tie to [`corp_conflict.scene.dry`](../background/corp_conflict.scene.dry) infra damage.\n\n### Destructive raid progress (war pairs)\n\nWhile faction **A** and **B** are tagged **at war**, each side keeps its own **raid progress** tracker (0–∞%, building toward strikes on the other). **Peace** resets both trackers to **0**.\n\n#### Monthly progress gain (each side)\n\n```\nmean = (strength_A + strength_B) / 2\nside_bonus = (strength_side / mean - 1) × bonus_rate    // 0 if side is smaller\nraw_gain_side = mean × (1 + side_bonus)\ngain_side = raw_gain_side / (LE / crime)               // citywide LE/crime; tune if district-local fits better\n```\n\n| War type | `bonus_rate` (larger side) | Progress multiplier |\n|----------|----------------------------|---------------------|\n| Default (syndicate–syndicate, corp–corp, …) | **5%** | ×1 |\n| **Syndicate vs corporation** | **25%** on the larger side (usually the corp) | **×1.6** on both sides' gains |\n\n`LE` and `crime` here are **general** public-order values (citywide `LE` sum or mean and `Q.crime_level` — pick one consistent definition at implementation). Higher order (large `LE / crime`) **slows** raid buildup.\n\nCheck thresholds **after** applying monthly gain (and after any same-month attrition).\n\n#### Raid triggers (attacker → target)\n\nUse [`Q.economicAssets`](../economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry) housing/asset counts **owned by the target faction**. District order for ties = [`DISTRICT_IDS`](../election_runtime.scene.dry) index (**Docks = 1** … **Deeps = 7**).\n\n| Progress | Condition | Target district | Effect |\n|----------|-----------|-----------------|--------|\n| **≥ 50%** | Target has **any housing** | District where target has the **most** housing | Housing destroyed (raid); ties → **lower** district number |\n| **≥ 100%** | Target has **any assets** | District where target has the **fewest** assets | Asset destroyed (raid); ties → **higher** district number; then **progress −= 100** |\n\n- Housing and asset raids can both fire as progress climbs (e.g. housing at 50%, asset at 100% in one buildup).\n- If the relevant condition fails (no housing at 50%, no assets at 100%), that threshold does nothing until the target holds stock.\n- Hook destruction through existing economic-asset APIs (`destroy` / housing bucket helpers in [`economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry`](../economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry)).\n\n#### Monthly raid report (UI)\n\nAt end of paramilitary tick, build `Q.monthly_raid_report`:\n\n- **Empty string** if nothing was destroyed this month.\n- Otherwise one line per raid: **`X blew up Y in Z`** (attacker label, housing/asset label, district name).\n\nDisplay at the **top of [`main.scene.dry`](../main.scene.dry)** via `[+ monthly_raid_report +]` (or raw HTML block). Clear or regenerate each month in `monthly_tick_phase1`.\n\n---\n\n## Political and prosperity effects\n\n**Per-district crime** (stratum-weighted exposure):\n\n- Background drain on voter-block prosperity — cooperatives and drones more secured; waves more vulnerable.\n- Electorate modifier on **D** from crime — **nonlinear:** at low `parochialism`, modest crime can slightly help democrats; runaway crime is a large liability.\n\n**City crime** drives both:\n\n- `parochialism` **up** (population rallies together).\n- `parochial_radicalism` **up** (same stress makes extremism more appealing).\n\n**Syndicate coercion:** per-syndicate `R` vs LE → district voter shift toward G; not rank growth.\n\n### Drone vote buying (separate system)\n\n**Not** derived from `R`. Combined syndicate affluence (`prosperity_families` + `edges` + `sharks`) → citywide drone stratum shift toward G / away from effective C.\n\n- **Implemented:** `Q.syncSyndicateDroneWealthStacks` + catalog rows in [`electorate_runtime.scene.dry`](../electorate_runtime.scene.dry).\n- **FUTURE:** per-syndicate prosperity → separate puppet-party modifiers.\n- Event spike: [`drone_vote_buying.dry`](../background/drone_vote_buying.dry) (`drone_syndicate_bribe_boost`) stacks on top.\n\n---\n\n## Exceptional events (out of band)\n\nBlind eye, raid heat, and similar beats **outside** the monthly band logic:\n\n- One-month flags (e.g. LE discounted vs one syndicate).\n- Instant QNM / attrition hits.\n- Temporary `crime_modifier` spikes decaying over 1–3 months.\n\nCable promises ([`cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry`](../major/cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry)) are the primary source; disband-militia guts LE on finalize.\n\n---\n\n## Card / stack hooks\n\n| Source | Hook |\n|--------|------|\n| [`security.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry) | Police QNM, loyalty, numbers; `crime_modifier` |\n| [`militia_degrade.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/militia_degrade.scene.dry) | Militia QNM; patrol flags → modifier |\n| [`community_outreach.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry) | `crime_relief_*` stacks |\n| Cable syndicate events | Shock flags + electorate stacks |\n| Attitude runtime | Leverage/reprisal → corp police in LE sum |\n| [`drone_vote_buying.dry`](../background/drone_vote_buying.dry) | Affluence bribery — outside paramilitary tick |\n\n---\n\n## Monthly tick order\n\n1. Apply narrative shock flags/deltas (if any).\n2. Prosperity → watch; parochialism nudge; punk floor.\n3. Syndicate/corp QNM from `prosperity_*` (slow institutional update only).\n4. Militias — lower quality, **more room to grow** via morale under sustained crime.\n\n---\n\n## Actors\n\n| Paramilitary | Patron | Role |\n|--------------|--------|------|\n| Syndicate muscle | Families, Edges, Sharks | District footprint; `prosperity_*` feeds QNM strength and (separately) drone bribery |\n| Corporate police | Soylent, Magrail, Brazos | Protect corp assets in home (and spill) districts |\n| City police | City government | Baseline public order; reform/defund changes QNM and loyalty |\n| Community militias | Democratic movement | Volunteer LE; lower starting quality, higher loyalty headroom |\n| Punks (name TBD) | None | Background outlaw strength when big players are quiet |\n| Watch | None (ambient) | Background LE from affluence / prosperity |\n\n**Rank dynamics:** syndicates and corps **do not** grow or shrink from the **LE balance** (dominance vs police/militia does not recruit or bleed ranks). Syndicate `prosperity_*` and future asset investment may expand ranks; corps hire from institutional budgets. Law enforcement does not face an ever-moving criminal headcount — only punks (and narrative shocks) drift on ambient conditions.\n\n**Exception:** syndicate **vs** syndicate war (open conflict) can cost **both** sides numbers and/or morale each month — the main way syndicate paramilitaries shrink outside narrative events.\n\n---\n\n## Building LE and outlaw mass\n\n### Public LE (per district)\n\n```\nLE = city_police + militia + watch + parochialism_nudge [+ corp_police_buff]\n```\n\n| Component | Source |\n|-----------|--------|\n| City police, militia | QNM strength in district |\n| **Watch** | Small bonus from population-weighted **district prosperity** |\n| Parochialism nudge | Very small LE boost from `Q.parochialism` (less than watch) |\n| Corp police buff | If leverage > reprisal: add `(3% × leverage) − (1% × reprisal)` of local corporate police strength (tune constants) |\n\n### Outlaw mass (per district)\n\n```\noutlaw_mass = sum(syndicate QNM in district) + punks\n```\n\nSyndicate `prosperity_*` and district G footprint feed syndicate QNM as **slow institutional inputs** (not monthly growth from beating LE). Mirror home-district links in [`PROSPERITY_IG_HOME_DISTRICT_LINKS`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry) (Families → Pitts + spill, Sharks → Deeps, etc.).\n\n### Dominance ratio\n\n```\nR = outlaw_mass / LE     (if LE <= 0, treat as collapsing)\n```\n\nSame ratio pattern reused for sub-matchups (corp assets, per-syndicate coercion) with their own thresholds where needed.\n\n---\n\n## Threshold bands\n\nDefault bands on **`R`** for public order. Dead zones between bands reduce monthly oscillation. Optional **hysteresis** (different cutoffs up vs down) if playtests show flip-flopping.\n\n### LE morale drift (police + militia)\n\nCompare **local** `R` with a **small citywide** spillover on the same bands.\n\n| Condition | Band | Effect |\n|-----------|------|--------|\n| `R < 0.20` | Secure | LE morale **rises** |\n| `0.20 ≤ R < 0.50` | Uneasy | Morale **steady** |\n| `0.50 ≤ R < 0.70` | Contested | LE morale **falls** |\n| `R ≥ 0.70` | Collapsing | Morale **falls** harder; civil-order-collapse effects |\n\nMilitia may use the same thresholds with faster step sizes. Low militia morale → [`militia_degrade.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/militia_degrade.scene.dry). [`security.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry) changes police QNM and loyalty.\n\n### Punks\n\nMorale/numbers drift **with** lawlessness (`R`), not from institutional budget.\n\n### District crime level (output)\n\nMap local `R` to `<district>_crime` (then blend city spillover below). Illustrative:\n\n| R | Crime band |\n|---|------------|\n| < 0.25 | Low |\n| 0.25 – 0.50 | Moderate |\n| 0.50 – 0.75 | High |\n| ≥ 0.75 | Severe |\n\nPlus `<district>_crime_modifier` stacks and minus `crime_relief_*` from [`community_outreach.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry).\n\n### City spillover\n\nEach district's **effective crime** ≈ **80% local + 20% city aggregate** (local control dominates).\n\n**City crime** = population-weighted average of district crime → `Q.crime_level`. Feeds tourism/longshore in [`organize_phase_tick.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry), [`PROSPERITY_PITTS_CRIME`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry), and citywide attitudes.\n\n### Other matchups (same ratio idea)\n\n| Matchup | Effect |\n|---------|--------|\n| Corp police vs local outlaw mass | Corp prosperity/affluence protected when corp dominates; narrowing gap reduces yield |\n| Each syndicate vs LE (+ enemy syndicate if at war) | Street coercion → district G shift; **not** rank growth |\n| Syndicate at war | Enemy strength added to LE **for that syndicate's coercion matchup only** (not general crime) |\n\n---\n\n## Open conflict\n\nWhen two paramilitaries are in **open conflict** (syndicate vs syndicate; corp vs corp while `cable_break_peace = 0`; syndicate vs corp):\n\n- Arithmetic **mean** of their QNM strengths → severity of violence, collateral damage, mutual attrition.\n- **Syndicate wars:** both sides lose numbers and/or morale proportional to intensity.\n- Corp wars: attrition TBD (morale/numbers and/or infra).\n- Collateral may tie to [`corp_conflict.scene.dry`](../background/corp_conflict.scene.dry) infra damage.\n\n### Destructive raid progress (war pairs)\n\nWhile faction **A** and **B** are tagged **at war**, each side keeps its own **raid progress** tracker (0–∞%, building toward strikes on the other). **Peace** resets both trackers to **0**.\n\n#### Monthly progress gain (each side)\n\n```\nmean = (strength_A + strength_B) / 2\nside_bonus = (strength_side / mean - 1) × bonus_rate    // 0 if side is smaller\nraw_gain_side = mean × (1 + side_bonus)\ngain_side = raw_gain_side / (LE / crime)               // citywide LE/crime; tune if district-local fits better\n```\n\n| War type | `bonus_rate` (larger side) | Progress multiplier |\n|----------|----------------------------|---------------------|\n| Default (syndicate–syndicate, corp–corp, …) | **5%** | ×1 |\n| **Syndicate vs corporation** | **25%** on the larger side (usually the corp) | **×1.6** on both sides' gains |\n\n`LE` and `crime` here are **general** public-order values (citywide `LE` sum or mean and `Q.crime_level` — pick one consistent definition at implementation). Higher order (large `LE / crime`) **slows** raid buildup.\n\nCheck thresholds **after** applying monthly gain (and after any same-month attrition).\n\n#### Raid triggers (attacker → target)\n\nUse [`Q.economicAssets`](../economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry) housing/asset counts **owned by the target faction**. District order for ties = [`DISTRICT_IDS`](../election_runtime.scene.dry) index (**Docks = 1** … **Deeps = 7**).\n\n| Progress | Condition | Target district | Effect |\n|----------|-----------|-----------------|--------|\n| **≥ 50%** | Target has **any housing** | District where target has the **most** housing | Housing destroyed (raid); ties → **lower** district number |\n| **≥ 100%** | Target has **any assets** | District where target has the **fewest** assets | Asset destroyed (raid); ties → **higher** district number; then **progress −= 100** |\n\n- Housing and asset raids can both fire as progress climbs (e.g. housing at 50%, asset at 100% in one buildup).\n- If the relevant condition fails (no housing at 50%, no assets at 100%), that threshold does nothing until the target holds stock.\n- Hook destruction through existing economic-asset APIs (`destroy` / housing bucket helpers in [`economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry`](../economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry)).\n\n#### Monthly raid report (UI)\n\nAt end of paramilitary tick, build `Q.monthly_raid_report`:\n\n- **Empty string** if nothing was destroyed this month.\n- Otherwise one line per raid: **`X blew up Y in Z`** (attacker label, housing/asset label, district name).\n\nDisplay at the **top of [`main.scene.dry`](../main.scene.dry)** via `[+ monthly_raid_report +]` (or raw HTML block). Clear or regenerate each month in `monthly_tick_phase1`.\n\n---\n\n## Political and prosperity effects\n\n**Per-district crime** (stratum-weighted exposure):\n\n- Background drain on voter-block prosperity — cooperatives and drones more secured; waves more vulnerable.\n- Electorate modifier on **D** from crime — **nonlinear:** at low `parochialism`, modest crime can slightly help democrats; runaway crime is a large liability.\n\n**City crime** drives both:\n\n- `parochialism` **up** (population rallies together).\n- `parochial_radicalism` **up** (same stress makes extremism more appealing).\n\n**Syndicate coercion:** per-syndicate `R` vs LE → district voter shift toward G; not rank growth.\n\n### Drone vote buying (separate system)\n\n**Not** derived from `R`. Combined syndicate affluence (`prosperity_families` + `edges` + `sharks`) → citywide drone stratum shift toward G / away from effective C.\n\n- **Implemented:** `Q.syncSyndicateDroneWealthStacks` + catalog rows in [`electorate_runtime.scene.dry`](../electorate_runtime.scene.dry).\n- **FUTURE:** per-syndicate prosperity → separate puppet-party modifiers.\n- Event spike: [`drone_vote_buying.dry`](../background/drone_vote_buying.dry) (`drone_syndicate_bribe_boost`) stacks on top.\n\n---\n\n## Exceptional events (out of band)\n\nBlind eye, raid heat, and similar beats **outside** the monthly band logic:\n\n- One-month flags (e.g. LE discounted vs one syndicate).\n- Instant QNM / attrition hits.\n- Temporary `crime_modifier` spikes decaying over 1–3 months.\n\nCable promises ([`cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry`](../major/cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry)) are the primary source; disband-militia guts LE on finalize.\n\n---\n\n## Card / stack hooks\n\n| Source | Hook |\n|--------|------|\n| [`security.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry) | Police QNM, loyalty, numbers; `crime_modifier` |\n| [`militia_degrade.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/militia_degrade.scene.dry) | Militia QNM; patrol flags → modifier |\n| [`community_outreach.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry) | `crime_relief_*` stacks |\n| Cable syndicate events | Shock flags + electorate stacks |\n| Attitude runtime | Leverage/reprisal → corp police in LE sum |\n| [`drone_vote_buying.dry`](../background/drone_vote_buying.dry) | Affluence bribery — outside paramilitary tick |\n\n---\n\n## Monthly tick order\n\n1. Apply narrative shock flags/deltas (if any).\n2. Prosperity → watch; parochialism nudge; punk floor.\n3. Syndicate/corp QNM from `prosperity_*` (slow institutional update only).\n4. Morale drift: police, militia (from `R` bands); punks.\n5. Open-conflict pairs → collateral + attrition; raid progress gain + threshold checks; apply housing/asset destruction; set `Q.monthly_raid_report`.\n6. `R` → per-district crime; blend ~20% city spillover.\n7. Population-weighted city crime → tourism, longshore, parochialism, parochial_radicalism.\n8. Crime → block prosperity drain (stratum weights).\n9. Syndicate coercion from per-matchup `R` (not rank change).\n10. Decay temporary event modifiers.\n\n**Outside this tick:** drone wealth stacks sync on `Q.applyElectorateModifiers` each projection.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation\n\n| Piece | Location |\n|-------|----------|\n| Runtime API | New block in [`organize_phase_tick.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry) or dedicated silent setup scene (`MIKASA_CRIME_PARAMILITARY_*`) |\n| District display | [`election_runtime.scene.dry`](../election_runtime.scene.dry) `syncDistrictDisplays()` reads ticked `<district>_crime`; retire `gPoll`/`hPoll` proxy |\n| Labels | [`crime.qdisplay.dry`](../../qdisplays/crime.qdisplay.dry) |\n| Corp war tick | Wire [`corp_conflict.scene.dry`](../background/corp_conflict.scene.dry) while `cable_break_peace = 0` |\n\n---\n\n## Open tuning (implementation-time)\n\n- Exact numeric cutoffs and hysteresis per band.\n- Coercion → poll shift magnitudes per syndicate.\n- Punks floor/ceiling; district specials (Deeps isolation, Docks patchwork).\n- Whether syndicate `prosperity_*` feeds Q, N, or both.\n- Corp-vs-corp attrition during cable war vs ceasefire.\n- Rebellion-phase loyalty on all paramilitaries.\n"
}

- **Progress gain:** based on arithmetic mean of QNM strengths; larger side gets `(strength/mean − 1) × bonus_rate` (5% default, **25%** for syndicate–corp); syndicate–corp gains **×1.6**; both sides divided by **LE/crime**

## [2026-06-08T13:15:38Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

Each runtime simply jumps to jumpScene. Setup_functions orchestrates the full chain during boot only.

Creating `crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry` with template functions. `qnmStrength` will accept qnm values or separate arguments. `safeRatio` will guard against zero denominators. Band classifiers like `publicOrderBand` and `corpAssetBand` will return strings for switch statements. The corp asset band compares corpPolice to outlaw, with higher ratios indicating stronger corporate dominance.

`calcPublicOrderBalance` will compute the ratio and band from LE and outlaw mass. `applyPublicOrderBalanceEffects` will translate that balance into scene effects. `syndicateCoercionBand` compares syndicate strength to law enforcement plus war allies. `conflictIntensityBand` will drive attrition tiers.

The `applyPublicOrderBalanceEffects` switch maps each public order band to specific scene effects. Secure raises morale drift and crime tier by one. Uneasy leaves morale unchanged but pushes crime tier to two. Contested drops morale drift by one and crime tier to three. Collapsing drives morale down by two, crime tier to four, and sets collapse to true.

Corp asset bands are protected, stressed, and breached. Syndicate coercion bands are suppressed, contested, and dominating. Conflict intensity bands are skirmish, heavy, and brutal. Raid progress gains will be calculated per side and returned with a slow, normal, or fast band based on order divisor.

Raid progress gain now uses a mean strength across both sides. Syndicate versus corporation mode applies a 0.25 bonus rate and 1.6 multiplier. The order divisor is LE divided by crime, defaulting to one if zero. A side gain helper will award bonus rate only to whichever side is larger.

The side gain formula applies bonus rate only when a side exceeds the mean strength. Final gain equals mean times bonus times multiplier divided by order divisor. Threshold effects will be handled by a separate `raidThresholdEffects` function keyed to progress, housing, and assets. Templates will be assigned to Q. Setup functions and documentation will be updated.

District crime bands use thresholds of 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75, while morale bands use 0.2, 0.5, and 0.7. Each balance will get its own apply function with a dedicated switch statement. One apply function can still set multiple effect fields in a single pass.

`crimeLevelBand` will classify public order using district thresholds while `moraleBand` keeps its own. Both share `calcPublicOrderBalance`. `applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects` will handle the morale switch. `applyPublicOrderCrimeEffects` will handle the crime tier switch.

{
  "file_path": "/home/airy/mikasa/source/scenes/planning/crime_paramilitary.md",
  "content": "# Crime & paramilitary system\n\n**Status:** design ready for implementation (Jun 2026). Replaces the display-only stub in `Q.syncDistrictDisplays()` and wires into `monthly_tick_phase1`.\n\n**Roadmap:** [`roadmap.md`](../../roadmap.md) — District crime (planned).\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nCrime and collateral damage from warfare flow through **paramilitary groups** — armed capacity tied to a patron (or to nobody). Each month, sum **law-enforcement strength** and **outlaw strength** per district, form a **dominance ratio** `R`, and apply **threshold bands** (no continuous curve). Narrative events (blind eye, raid heat, …) apply **sudden out-of-band shocks** rather than slowly rewriting background levels.\n\n**Terminology:**\n\n| Term | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| **QNM** | **Q**uality, **N**umbers, **M**orale — the three stats that multiply into faction strength |\n| **LE** | Law-enforcement strength in a district (public order side) |\n| **Outlaw mass** | Criminal strength (syndicates + punks) |\n| **`R`** | `outlaw_mass / LE` — dominance ratio |\n| **District crime** | Output label (1–10, [`crime.qdisplay.dry`](../../qdisplays/crime.qdisplay.dry)) derived from `R` bands |\n| **Watch** | Background LE from district prosperity (flip side of punks) |\n\n---\n\n## QNM\n\nEach paramilitary has **quality**, **numbers**, **morale**, and **loyalty**.\n\n- **Strength** = `Q × N × M`\n- **Loyalty** caps how high morale can rise (rebellion phase later; already matters for police vs militia).\n\n**Starting posture:** city police — higher quality, **lower loyalty** (brittle, corruptible). Militias — lower quality, **more room to grow** via morale under sustained crime.\n\n---\n\n## Actors\n\n| Paramilitary | Patron | Role |\n|--------------|--------|------|\n| Syndicate muscle | Families, Edges, Sharks | District footprint; `prosperity_*` feeds QNM strength and (separately) drone bribery |\n| Corporate police | Soylent, Magrail, Brazos | Protect corp assets in home (and spill) districts |\n| City police | City government | Baseline public order; reform/defund changes QNM and loyalty |\n| Community militias | Democratic movement | Volunteer LE; lower starting quality, higher loyalty headroom |\n| Punks (name TBD) | None | Background outlaw strength when big players are quiet |\n| Watch | None (ambient) | Background LE from affluence / prosperity |\n\n**Rank dynamics:** syndicates and corps **do not** grow or shrink from the **LE balance** (dominance vs police/militia does not recruit or bleed ranks). Syndicate `prosperity_*` and future asset investment may expand ranks; corps hire from institutional budgets. Law enforcement does not face an ever-moving criminal headcount — only punks (and narrative shocks) drift on ambient conditions.\n\n**Exception:** syndicate **vs** syndicate war (open conflict) can cost **both** sides numbers and/or morale each month — the main way syndicate paramilitaries shrink outside narrative events.\n\n---\n\n## Building LE and outlaw mass\n\n### Public LE (per district)\n\n```\nLE = city_police + militia + watch + parochialism_nudge [+ corp_police_buff]\n```\n\n| Component | Source |\n|-----------|--------|\n| City police, militia | QNM strength in district |\n| **Watch** | Small bonus from population-weighted **district prosperity** |\n| Parochialism nudge | Very small LE boost from `Q.parochialism` (less than watch) |\n| Corp police buff | If leverage > reprisal: add `(3% × leverage) − (1% × reprisal)` of local corporate police strength (tune constants) |\n\n### Outlaw mass (per district)\n\n```\noutlaw_mass = sum(syndicate QNM in district) + punks\n```\n\nSyndicate `prosperity_*` and district G footprint feed syndicate QNM as **slow institutional inputs** (not monthly growth from beating LE). Mirror home-district links in [`PROSPERITY_IG_HOME_DISTRICT_LINKS`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry) (Families → Pitts + spill, Sharks → Deeps, etc.).\n\n### Dominance ratio\n\n```\nR = outlaw_mass / LE     (if LE <= 0, treat as collapsing)\n```\n\nSame ratio pattern reused for sub-matchups (corp assets, per-syndicate coercion) with their own thresholds where needed.\n\n---\n\n## Threshold bands\n\nDefault bands on **`R`** for public order. Dead zones between bands reduce monthly oscillation. Optional **hysteresis** (different cutoffs up vs down) if playtests show flip-flopping.\n\n### LE morale drift (police + militia)\n\nCompare **local** `R` with a **small citywide** spillover on the same bands.\n\n| Condition | Band | Effect |\n|-----------|------|--------|\n| `R < 0.20` | Secure | LE morale **rises** |\n| `0.20 ≤ R < 0.50` | Uneasy | Morale **steady** |\n| `0.50 ≤ R < 0.70` | Contested | LE morale **falls** |\n| `R ≥ 0.70` | Collapsing | Morale **falls** harder; civil-order-collapse effects |\n\nMilitia may use the same thresholds with faster step sizes. Low militia morale → [`militia_degrade.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/militia_degrade.scene.dry). [`security.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry) changes police QNM and loyalty.\n\n### Punks\n\nMorale/numbers drift **with** lawlessness (`R`), not from institutional budget.\n\n### District crime level (output)\n\nMap local `R` to `<district>_crime` (then blend city spillover below). Illustrative:\n\n| R | Crime band |\n|---|------------|\n| < 0.25 | Low |\n| 0.25 – 0.50 | Moderate |\n| 0.50 – 0.75 | High |\n| ≥ 0.75 | Severe |\n\nPlus `<district>_crime_modifier` stacks and minus `crime_relief_*` from [`community_outreach.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry).\n\n### City spillover\n\nEach district's **effective crime** ≈ **80% local + 20% city aggregate** (local control dominates).\n\n**City crime** = population-weighted average of district crime → `Q.crime_level`. Feeds tourism/longshore in [`organize_phase_tick.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry), [`PROSPERITY_PITTS_CRIME`](../cards/local_organizing/organize_phase_tick.scene.dry), and citywide attitudes.\n\n### Other matchups (same ratio idea)\n\n| Matchup | Effect |\n|---------|--------|\n| Corp police vs local outlaw mass | Corp prosperity/affluence protected when corp dominates; narrowing gap reduces yield |\n| Each syndicate vs LE (+ enemy syndicate if at war) | Street coercion → district G shift; **not** rank growth |\n| Syndicate at war | Enemy strength added to LE **for that syndicate's coercion matchup only** (not general crime) |\n\n---\n\n## Open conflict\n\nWhen two paramilitaries are in **open conflict** (syndicate vs syndicate; corp vs corp while `cable_break_peace = 0`; syndicate vs corp):\n\n- Arithmetic **mean** of their QNM strengths → severity of violence, collateral damage, mutual attrition.\n- **Syndicate wars:** both sides lose numbers and/or morale proportional to intensity.\n- Corp wars: attrition TBD (morale/numbers and/or infra).\n- Collateral may tie to [`corp_conflict.scene.dry`](../background/corp_conflict.scene.dry) infra damage.\n\n### Destructive raid progress (war pairs)\n\nWhile faction **A** and **B** are tagged **at war**, each side keeps its own **raid progress** tracker (0–∞%, building toward strikes on the other). **Peace** resets both trackers to **0**.\n\n#### Monthly progress gain (each side)\n\n```\nmean = (strength_A + strength_B) / 2\nside_bonus = (strength_side / mean - 1) × bonus_rate    // 0 if side is smaller\nraw_gain_side = mean × (1 + side_bonus)\ngain_side = raw_gain_side / (LE / crime)               // citywide LE/crime; tune if district-local fits better\n```\n\n| War type | `bonus_rate` (larger side) | Progress multiplier |\n|----------|----------------------------|---------------------|\n| Default (syndicate–syndicate, corp–corp, …) | **5%** | ×1 |\n| **Syndicate vs corporation** | **25%** on the larger side (usually the corp) | **×1.6** on both sides' gains |\n\n`LE` and `crime` here are **general** public-order values (citywide `LE` sum or mean and `Q.crime_level` — pick one consistent definition at implementation). Higher order (large `LE / crime`) **slows** raid buildup.\n\nCheck thresholds **after** applying monthly gain (and after any same-month attrition).\n\n#### Raid triggers (attacker → target)\n\nUse [`Q.economicAssets`](../economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry) housing/asset counts **owned by the target faction**. District order for ties = [`DISTRICT_IDS`](../election_runtime.scene.dry) index (**Docks = 1** … **Deeps = 7**).\n\n| Progress | Condition | Target district | Effect |\n|----------|-----------|-----------------|--------|\n| **≥ 50%** | Target has **any housing** | District where target has the **most** housing | Housing destroyed (raid); ties → **lower** district number |\n| **≥ 100%** | Target has **any assets** | District where target has the **fewest** assets | Asset destroyed (raid); ties → **higher** district number; then **progress −= 100** |\n\n- Housing and asset raids can both fire as progress climbs (e.g. housing at 50%, asset at 100% in one buildup).\n- If the relevant condition fails (no housing at 50%, no assets at 100%), that threshold does nothing until the target holds stock.\n- Hook destruction through existing economic-asset APIs (`destroy` / housing bucket helpers in [`economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry`](../economic_assets_runtime.scene.dry)).\n\n#### Monthly raid report (UI)\n\nAt end of paramilitary tick, build `Q.monthly_raid_report`:\n\n- **Empty string** if nothing was destroyed this month.\n- Otherwise one line per raid: **`X blew up Y in Z`** (attacker label, housing/asset label, district name).\n\nDisplay at the **top of [`main.scene.dry`](../main.scene.dry)** via `[+ monthly_raid_report +]` (or raw HTML block). Clear or regenerate each month in `monthly_tick_phase1`.\n\n---\n\n## Political and prosperity effects\n\n**Per-district crime** (stratum-weighted exposure):\n\n- Background drain on voter-block prosperity — cooperatives and drones more secured; waves more vulnerable.\n- Electorate modifier on **D** from crime — **nonlinear:** at low `parochialism`, modest crime can slightly help democrats; runaway crime is a large liability.\n\n**City crime** drives both:\n\n- `parochialism` **up** (population rallies together).\n- `parochial_radicalism` **up** (same stress makes extremism more appealing).\n\n**Syndicate coercion:** per-syndicate `R` vs LE → district voter shift toward G; not rank growth.\n\n### Drone vote buying (separate system)\n\n**Not** derived from `R`. Combined syndicate affluence (`prosperity_families` + `edges` + `sharks`) → citywide drone stratum shift toward G / away from effective C.\n\n- **Implemented:** `Q.syncSyndicateDroneWealthStacks` + catalog rows in [`electorate_runtime.scene.dry`](../electorate_runtime.scene.dry).\n- **FUTURE:** per-syndicate prosperity → separate puppet-party modifiers.\n- Event spike: [`drone_vote_buying.dry`](../background/drone_vote_buying.dry) (`drone_syndicate_bribe_boost`) stacks on top.\n\n---\n\n## Exceptional events (out of band)\n\nBlind eye, raid heat, and similar beats **outside** the monthly band logic:\n\n- One-month flags (e.g. LE discounted vs one syndicate).\n- Instant QNM / attrition hits.\n- Temporary `crime_modifier` spikes decaying over 1–3 months.\n\nCable promises ([`cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry`](../major/cable_break_negotiations.scene.dry)) are the primary source; disband-militia guts LE on finalize.\n\n---\n\n## Card / stack hooks\n\n| Source | Hook |\n|--------|------|\n| [`security.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/security.scene.dry) | Police QNM, loyalty, numbers; `crime_modifier` |\n| [`militia_degrade.scene.dry`](../cards/city_affairs/militia_degrade.scene.dry) | Militia QNM; patrol flags → modifier |\n| [`community_outreach.scene.dry`](../cards/local_organizing/community_outreach.scene.dry) | `crime_relief_*` stacks |\n| Cable syndicate events | Shock flags + electorate stacks |\n| Attitude runtime | Leverage/reprisal → corp police in LE sum |\n| [`drone_vote_buying.dry`](../background/drone_vote_buying.dry) | Affluence bribery — outside paramilitary tick |\n\n---\n\n## Monthly tick order\n\n1. Apply narrative shock flags/deltas (if any).\n2. Prosperity → watch; parochialism nudge; punk floor.\n3. Syndicate/corp QNM from `prosperity_*` (slow institutional update only).\n4. Morale drift: police, militia (from `R` bands); punks.\n5. Open-conflict pairs → collateral + attrition; raid progress gain + threshold checks; apply housing/asset destruction; set `Q.monthly_raid_report`.\n6. `R` → per-district crime; blend ~20% city spillover.\n7. Population-weighted city crime → tourism, longshore, parochialism, parochial_radicalism.\n8. Crime → block prosperity drain (stratum weights).\n9. Syndicate coercion from per-matchup `R` (not rank change).\n10. Decay temporary event modifiers.\n\n**Outside this tick:** drone wealth stacks sync on `Q.applyElectorateModifiers` each projection.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation\n\n| Piece | Location |\n|-------|----------|\n| Runtime API | [`crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry`](../crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry) — `calc*` + `apply*` template pairs (`MIKASA_CRIME_PARAMILITARY_*`); monthly tick still hooks from `monthly_tick_phase1` |\n| District display | [`election_runtime.scene.dry`](../election_runtime.scene.dry) `syncDistrictDisplays()` reads ticked `<district>_crime`; retire `gPoll`/`hPoll` proxy |\n| Labels | [`crime.qdisplay.dry`](../../qdisplays/crime.qdisplay.dry) |\n| Corp war tick | Wire [`corp_conflict.scene.dry`](../background/corp_conflict.scene.dry) while `cable_break_peace = 0` |\n| Raid report UI | Top of [`main.scene.dry`](../main.scene.dry) — `Q.monthly_raid_report` |\n\n---\n\n## Open tuning (implementation-time)\n\n- Exact numeric cutoffs and hysteresis per band.\n- Raid progress scale (whether `mean` needs a coefficient so 50%/100% land on sensible month counts).\n- Citywide vs district `LE / crime` divisor for raid buildup.\n- Whether crossing 50% housing resets or only fires once per war.\n- Coercion → poll shift magnitudes per syndicate.\n- Punks floor/ceiling; district specials (Deeps isolation, Docks patchwork).\n- Whether syndicate `prosperity_*` feeds Q, N, or both.\n- Corp-vs-corp attrition during cable war vs ceasefire.\n- Rebellion-phase loyalty on all paramilitaries.\n"
}

## [2026-06-08T13:16:50Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Added [`source/scenes/crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry`](source/scenes/crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry) with separate **calc → apply** pairs, each apply using a **`switch` on a band string**. Bootstrapped via [`setup_functions.scene.dry`](source/scenes/setup_functions.scene.dry).

### Shared helpers
- `Q.qnmStrength(qnm)` — `Q × N × M`
- `Q.dominanceRatio(offense, defense)` — ratio for `R`-style balances

### Balance pairs

| Calculate | Apply (switch on band) |
|-----------|-------------------------|
| `calcPublicOrderBalance({ le, outlawMass })` | `applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects` — `secure` / `uneasy` / `contested` / `collapsing` |
| same | `applyPublicOrderCrimeEffects` — `low` / `moderate` / `high` / `severe` |
| `calcCorpAssetBalance({ corpPolice, outlawMass })` | `applyCorpAssetBalanceEffects` — `protected` → `lost` |
| `calcSyndicateCoercionBalance({ syndicateStrength, le, warAllyStrength })` | `applySyndicateCoercionEffects` — `suppressed` → `rampant` |
| `calcConflictIntensityBalance({ strengthA, strengthB })` | `applyConflictIntensityEffects` — `skirmish` → `total_war` |
| `calcRaidProgressGain({ strengthSide, strengthOther, le, crime, syndicateVsCorp })` | `applyRaidProgressEffects({ progress, hasHousing, hasAssets })` — `building` / `housing_threshold` / `asset_threshold` |

All effect functions return plain objects (deltas, flags, placeholder numbers) — **no state writes yet**. Threshold constants are at the top of the runtime block for tuning.

Monthly tick wiring is still TODO; these are templates ready to call from `monthly_tick_phase1`. Lint and `make-html` pass.

## [2026-06-08T13:19:55Z] assistant_thought (afterAgentThought)

The user wants advice on structuring returns for switch functions that yield both a string and a numerical value. They find designing these returns fiddly and want best practices to consider.

Calculation functions should return inputs, ratio, and band. Application functions should return band and magnitude. Avoid duplicating band if the caller trusts the balance. The numerical value could be a tier index, continuous strength, primary effect magnitude, or multiple effect fields. A common pattern is a structured object with band, tier, and magnitude.

A minimal `{ label, value }` pair is another viable structure. A table-driven approach can replace switches by mapping bands directly to rows in a constant object. Each apply function should return exactly one primary scalar when possible, such as `magnitude` or `severity`, to avoid choosing between competing effect deltas. Ordinal tiers should remain separate from display band strings; qdisplay can map tiers to labels while band strings stay for developer logs.

Magnitude should be derived from the ratio in the calculation step rather than inside the switch. The switch only needs to pick the band bucket, and interpolation handles values in between.

If the tier is simply the index of the band enum, returning both fields from the same switch case is acceptable.

Avoid mixing unrelated numbers in a single return. When several values belong together, group them under a named object such as `effects` alongside a summary scalar.

Use descriptive field names instead of magic keys like `value`.

A factory helper such as `bandResult(band, magnitude, extra)` can build the return object automatically from the band name.

In Mikasa, the calculation step should own the ratio, band, and optional continuous severity. The apply switch should then return `{ band, magnitude }` where magnitude is the exact number the tick will apply. Context logic should handle side effects like militia multipliers.

For crime, a concrete return might be `{ band, districtCrime, crimeTier }`, where `districtCrime` is the primary magnitude and `crimeTier` is the ordinal label index.

## [2026-06-08T13:20:14Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

The fiddliness usually comes from mixing three different jobs in one return: **label for humans**, **bucket for rules**, and **number for math**. Split those explicitly and it gets much easier.

## Recommended shape

For each `apply*` function, return a small fixed core plus optional extras:

```javascript
{
  band: 'contested',      // string — UI, logs, qdisplay lookup
  tier: 2,                // integer 0..n-1 — ordinal severity (stable for saves/compare)
  magnitude: -1,          // single primary scalar this effect cares about
  // optional:
  details: { ... }        // only when one band truly needs multiple numbers
}
```

**Rule of thumb:** one `apply*` → one **`magnitude`** meaning. If you need two unrelated numbers (e.g. housing raid *and* asset raid), that's two `apply*` calls or `details`, not two competing “main” values.

### Who computes what

| Layer | Returns |
|-------|---------|
| **`calc*`** | Inputs, `ratio`, `band` (and optionally a **continuous** 0–1 severity from ratio) |
| **`apply*`** | `band`, `tier`, `magnitude` (from switch/table) |

Keep **band classification in `calc*`** (or a shared `*Band(ratio)` helper). The switch in `apply*` should mostly map **band → numbers**, not re-derive bands from ratio. That way you never wonder “did we use the same thresholds in two places?”

### What `magnitude` should be per effect

Pick one clear unit per function:

| Function | Good `magnitude` | `tier` use |
|----------|------------------|------------|
| `applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects` | morale delta (e.g. `+1`, `0`, `-1`, `-2`) | 0=secure … 3=collapsing |
| `applyPublicOrderCrimeEffects` | `districtCrime` (1–10) | 0=low … 3=severe |
| `applyCorpAssetBalanceEffects` | `yieldMultiplier` | 0=protected … 3=lost |
| `applySyndicateCoercionEffects` | `pollShiftG` | 0=suppressed … 3=rampant |
| `applyConflictIntensityEffects` | `collateral` or a single `severity` | 0=skirmish … 3=total_war |
| `applyRaidProgressEffects` | `progressAfter` delta or `gain` applied | threshold band |

`details` is for when magnitude isn't enough — e.g. morale returns `magnitude: -1` for police and `details: { militia: -1.5 }` from `ctx.militiaMoraleMultiplier`.

## Why `tier` as well as `band`

Strings are great for prose; integers are great for code:

- Compare severity: `tier >= 2`
- Feed qdisplays: `[+ crime_tier : crime +]` without string parsing
- Avoid typos: `'contested'` vs `'Contested'`

Define once:

```javascript
var PUBLIC_ORDER_MORALE_TIER = {
  secure: 0, uneasy: 1, contested: 2, collapsing: 3,
}
```

Switch sets both:

```javascript
case 'contested':
  tier = 2
  magnitude = -1
  break
```

## Switch vs lookup table

If the fiddle is “what number goes with what band”, **tables often beat switches** for tuning:

```javascript
var PUBLIC_ORDER_MORALE_EFFECT = {
  secure:     { tier: 0, magnitude:  1 },
  uneasy:     { tier: 1, magnitude:  0 },
  contested:  { tier: 2, magnitude: -1 },
  collapsing: { tier: 3, magnitude: -2 },
}

function applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects(balance, ctx) {
  var row = PUBLIC_ORDER_MORALE_EFFECT[balance.moraleBand] || { tier: 1, magnitude: 0 }
  return {
    band: balance.moraleBand,
    tier: row.tier,
    magnitude: row.magnitude,
    details: {
      militia: row.magnitude * (ctx.militiaMoraleMultiplier || 1.5),
    },
  }
}
```

Same structure everywhere; balance designers edit tables, not control flow.

## Continuous vs stepped (optional)

Threshold **bands** for discrete effects; **ratio** for smooth effects if you want:

```javascript
// in calcPublicOrderBalance
severity: clamp((ratio - 0.2) / 0.5, 0, 1)  // 0 inside secure, 1 at collapsing
```

Then:

- **Switch/table** → band + tier + stepped `magnitude`
- **`severity`** → multiply or interpolate: `magnitude = baseMagnitude * (0.5 + 0.5 * severity)`

Use stepped-only until playtests ask for smoothness — fewer knobs.

## Small helper (consistent shape)

```javascript
function bandEffect(band, tier, magnitude, details) {
  var out = { band: band, tier: tier, magnitude: magnitude }
  if (details) { out.details = details }
  return out
}
```

Every `apply*` returns through this; callers always know where to look.

## Anti-patterns (what makes it fiddly)

1. **Different functions using `value` for different units** — always name it (`magnitude`, `yieldMultiplier`, `pollShiftG`).
2. **Band only in `apply*`, ratio only in `calc*`, no link** — log or return `ratio` on the effect object when debugging: `{ band, tier, magnitude, ratio: balance.ratio }`.
3. **One mega-return with every possible field** — split by effect type (you already have separate functions; keep separate return shapes).
4. **Modifiers in the switch** — `crime_modifier` belongs *after* apply: `districtCrime = effect.magnitude + modifier`, not inside the band table.

## Practical recommendation for Mikasa

Stick with your **calc / apply split**, and standardize apply returns as:

```javascript
{ band, tier, magnitude, ratio?, details? }
```

Refactor switches into **band → `{ tier, magnitude }` tables** at the top of `crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry`. Monthly tick code becomes:

```javascript
var balance = Q.calcPublicOrderBalance({ le, outlawMass })
var morale = Q.applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects(balance, ctx)
policeMorale += morale.magnitude
militiaMorale += morale.details.militia
```

That’s enough structure that you’re not re-deciding the return shape every time you add a new balance type.

I can refactor the runtime scene to this `{ band, tier, magnitude }` + table pattern if you want it in source next.

## [2026-06-08T13:24:09Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

For continuous values, treat **classification** (bands) and **interpolation** (smooth numbers) as separate layers, each with its own small functions when inline math gets hairy.

## The split

```
ratio (raw)
    → continuousSeverity(ratio, spec)   // 0..1 or domain range — can be multi-step
    → *Band(ratio)                      // stepped label — stays simple thresholds
    → apply* uses band table for base magnitude
    → optional: magnitude *= f(severity) or lerp between band anchors
```

**`calc*`** orchestrates and returns everything downstream needs:

```javascript
{
  ratio: 0.58,
  band: 'contested',      // from simple threshold helper
  severity: 0.76,         // from curve helper
}
```

**`apply*`** stays dumb: band → `{ tier, magnitude }`, then optionally scales by `severity` if you want smoothness inside a band.

---

## When inline is enough vs extract

| Inline is fine | Extract a named function |
|----------------|------------------------|
| `clamp((r - a) / (b - a), 0, 1)` one line | Piecewise linear across 3+ breakpoints |
| One ratio in, one number out | Multiple inputs (local `R` + city spillover) |
| Same formula once | Same curve reused (morale + punks + raid divisor) |

Rule: **extract when you can name the curve** (“public order severity from R”) or when the spec has more than ~2 breakpoints.

---

## Organization inside `crime_paramilitary_runtime.scene.dry`

Keep one runtime file but use **sections** (matches your `MIKASA_*` style):

```text
// 1. Generic math (reusable, no game meaning)
clamp, lerp, piecewiseLinear, normalizeRatio

// 2. Curve specs (data only — tune here)
PUBLIC_ORDER_SEVERITY_SPEC = { breakpoints: [...] }

// 3. Domain severity functions (ratio + spec → number)
publicOrderSeverity(ratio)
corpAssetPressure(ratio)

// 4. Band classifiers (ratio → string)
publicOrderMoraleBand(ratio)

// 5. calc* orchestrators (call severity + band, return bundle)
calcPublicOrderBalance(opts)

// 6. Effect tables + apply*
```

**Generic layer** — tiny, stable, copy-paste safe:

```javascript
function clamp01(x) {
    var n = Number(x)
    if (isNaN(n)) { return 0 }
    if (n < 0) { return 0 }
    if (n > 1) { return 1 }
    return n
}

function lerp(a, b, t) {
    return a + (b - a) * clamp01(t)
}

/** breakpoints: [{ at: 0.2, value: 0 }, { at: 0.7, value: 1 }, ...] sorted by at */
function piecewiseLinear(x, breakpoints) {
    var n = Number(x)
    if (isNaN(n) || !breakpoints || !breakpoints.length) { return 0 }
    if (n <= breakpoints[0].at) { return breakpoints[0].value }
    var last = breakpoints[breakpoints.length - 1]
    if (n >= last.at) { return last.value }
    for (var i = 1; i < breakpoints.length; i++) {
        var hi = breakpoints[i]
        var lo = breakpoints[i - 1]
        if (n <= hi.at) {
            var span = hi.at - lo.at
            if (span <= 0) { return hi.value }
            var t = (n - lo.at) / span
            return lerp(lo.value, hi.value, t)
        }
    }
    return last.value
}
```

**Spec as data** — balance lives in tables, not control flow:

```javascript
var PUBLIC_ORDER_SEVERITY_SPEC = {
    // ratio breakpoints → severity 0..1
    breakpoints: [
        { at: 0.00, value: 0.0 },
        { at: 0.20, value: 0.0 },  // flat “secure” floor
        { at: 0.50, value: 0.45 },
        { at: 0.70, value: 0.75 },
        { at: 1.00, value: 1.0 },
    ],
}

function publicOrderSeverity(ratio) {
    return piecewiseLinear(ratio, PUBLIC_ORDER_SEVERITY_SPEC.breakpoints)
}
```

When a curve gets **weird** (parochialism nudge, city spillover), don’t grow one function — add a **composer**:

```javascript
function publicOrderSeverityForDistrict(opts) {
    var local = publicOrderSeverity(opts.localRatio)
    var city = publicOrderSeverity(opts.cityRatio)
    var spill = Number(opts.citySpillover) || 0.2
    return clamp01(local * (1 - spill) + city * spill)
}
```

`calcPublicOrderBalance` only calls that composer and packs the result.

---

## Connecting continuous → discrete effects

Three patterns, from simplest to most flexible:

**A. Severity only for display / debug**  
Bands drive everything; `severity` is informational until you need smoothness.

**B. Scale the band’s magnitude** (good default):

```javascript
var base = PUBLIC_ORDER_MORALE_EFFECT[balance.moraleBand].magnitude
var magnitude = base * (0.5 + 0.5 * balance.severity)  // never quite zero in contested
```

**C. Lerp between band anchor values** (smooth across boundaries):

```javascript
// anchors at band midpoints, not switch cases
var magnitude = piecewiseLinear(balance.ratio, MORALE_MAGNITUDE_ANCHORS)
```

Use **B** when bands are the source of truth; **C** when you want the number to move every month as `R` drifts.

---

## If it outgrows one file

You’re on `.dry` runtime scenes, not `source/lib/*.js` for gameplay — so prefer **one silent scene, multiple named sections** over splitting files until it’s enormous.

If it does grow:

| Piece | Where |
|-------|--------|
| `clamp` / `lerp` / `piecewiseLinear` | top of runtime block (or shared if another system needs them) |
| `*_SPEC` breakpoint tables | next section — comment per curve |
| `*Severity(ratio, opts)` | one function per **meaning** (public order, corp pressure, raid buildup) |
| `calc*` | thin: gather inputs → call severity + band → return object |
| `apply*` | tables only; optional `scaleBySeverity(effect, severity)` one-liner |

Avoid a single `computeEverything(district)` — you already split by balance type; keep that.

---

## Return shape from `calc*` when continuous is involved

```javascript
return {
  // inputs (debug)
  le: le,
  outlawMass: outlawMass,
  ratio: ratio,
  // stepped
  moraleBand: publicOrderMoraleBand(ratio),
  crimeBand: publicOrderCrimeBand(ratio),
  // continuous
  severity: publicOrderSeverity(ratio),
}
```

`apply*` receives `balance` and uses `balance.moraleBand` + `balance.severity` without recomputing curves.

---

## Practical heuristics (the “not fiddly” part)

1. **One continuous output per curve function** — if you need two numbers, two functions or a `{ severity, pressure }` object with named fields, not `value1`/`value2`.
2. **Specs are JSON-like literals** — edit breakpoints without touching logic.
3. **Bands and curves share breakpoints when possible** — e.g. morale bands at 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.7; severity spec uses the same `at` values so docs and code stay aligned.
4. **Compose at calc, not apply** — apply reads finished `severity`; it doesn’t know about city spillover.
5. **Test with round ratios** — `R = 0.2, 0.49, 0.5, 0.69, 0.7` and log `{ band, severity, magnitude }` once in dev.

That’s the organization I’d use: **generic math → spec tables → named severity functions → thin calc* → table-driven apply***. Inline the one-liner `clamp((r-lo)/(hi-lo))`; extract as soon as you want a second curve or a second input to the same curve.

## [2026-06-08T13:26:08Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

The **composer** is the function that answers: “given everything we know about this district *this month*, what is the **single severity number** we feed into effects?” It sits **between** raw inputs and `calc*` / `apply*`.

Single-input curves are simple:

```text
localRatio  →  publicOrderSeverity(localRatio)  →  0..1
```

A composer is for when severity is **not** a pure function of one ratio:

```text
localRatio, cityRatio, spillover, modifiers…  →  composePublicOrderSeverity(...)  →  0..1
```

---

## Why not put that logic in `calc*` or `apply*`?

**`calcPublicOrderBalance`** should gather inputs and attach labels (`ratio`, `band`, `severity`). If you stuff spillover math in there, every balance type’s calc grows differently.

**`applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects`** should map **band → magnitude**. If it also blends local vs city, you can’t reuse the same apply for “local only” debug or for a future card that ignores city mood.

The composer owns **“how signals combine”**; band classifiers own **“which bucket”**; apply tables own **“what the bucket does.”**

```text
inputs
  → calc* (assemble raw numbers)
  → composer (blend → one severity)
  → band helper (same inputs or composed severity → string)
  → apply* (band → tier + magnitude, optional × severity)
```

---

## What a composer actually does

Three jobs, often all in one small function:

1. **Normalize** — turn each input into the same kind of number (usually 0..1 severity).
2. **Weight** — decide how much each input matters.
3. **Combine** — add, max, min, or layered mix.

### Example: local crime + city spillover (from your design)

```javascript
function composePublicOrderSeverity(opts) {
    opts = opts || {}
    var local = publicOrderSeverity(opts.localRatio)
    var city = publicOrderSeverity(opts.cityRatio)
    var spill = Number(opts.citySpillover)
    if (isNaN(spill)) { spill = 0.2 }

    // 80% local mood, 20% city — same idea as crime display blend
    return clamp01(local * (1 - spill) + city * spill)
}
```

`calcPublicOrderBalance` might look like:

```javascript
function calcPublicOrderBalance(opts) {
    var le = Number(opts.le) || 0
    var outlawMass = Number(opts.outlawMass) || 0
    var localRatio = dominanceRatio(outlawMass, le)

    var severity = composePublicOrderSeverity({
        localRatio: localRatio,
        cityRatio: opts.cityRatio,
        citySpillover: opts.citySpillover,
    })

    return {
        le: le,
        outlawMass: outlawMass,
        ratio: localRatio,
        severity: severity,
        moraleBand: publicOrderMoraleBand(localRatio),  // often still LOCAL for bands
        crimeBand: publicOrderCrimeBand(localRatio),
    }
}
```

Note the split: **severity** can be blended; **bands** often stay **local** so “Pitts is contested” stays true even if citywide order is okay. That’s a design choice — document it per effect:

| Effect | Band from | Severity from |
|--------|-----------|----------------|
| Morale drift | local `R` (+ tiny city nudge in composer) | composed |
| District crime label | local `R` | composed optional for fine-tuning |
| City `parochialism` | city aggregate | city only |

Composers make that table easy to implement without duplicating blend formulas.

---

## Common composition patterns

### 1. Weighted average (your spillover)

Good when inputs are the **same type** (two severities).

```text
result = w1·A + w2·B   (w1 + w2 = 1)
```

Use for: local vs city, “official LE” vs “felt” crime.

### 2. Max / “worst of”

```text
result = max(localSeverity, citySeverity * spill)
```

Good when **any** bad neighborhood taints morale even if the blend would look fine. Harsher than weighted average.

### 3. Base + bonus

```text
result = clamp01(baseSeverity + parochialismNudge + eventModifier)
```

Good when continuous curves are **mostly one ratio**, and other qualities are small shifts. Keep nudges in the composer, not in the breakpoint table.

```javascript
function composePublicOrderSeverity(opts) {
    var base = publicOrderSeverity(opts.localRatio)
    var parochial = (Number(opts.parochialism) || 0) * 0.0005  // tiny LE-like boost as lower severity
    var relief = (Number(opts.crimeRelief) || 0) * 0.05
    return clamp01(base - parochial + relief)
}
```

### 4. Layered (pipeline)

Output of one composer becomes input to another — only when stages have clear meaning:

```text
rawSeverity → applyPeaceDamping → applyEventShocks → finalSeverity
```

```javascript
function composeRaidProgressSeverity(opts) {
    var base = raidIntensitySeverity(opts.meanStrength)
    var order = orderCrimeDivisor(opts.le, opts.crime)
    // high order slows raids — divide gain, or map divisor → 0..1 dampener
    var damp = clamp01(2 / order)  // tune heavily
    return base * damp
}
```

### 5. Separate composers per **question**

Don’t one composer to rule them all:

- `composePublicOrderSeverity` — how bad does order feel?
- `composeCorpAssetPressure` — how threatened are holdings?
- `composeMoraleDriftSignal` — what should police/militia morale hear?

They may share sub-curves (`publicOrderSeverity`) but combine inputs differently.

---

## What goes in `opts` vs hardcoded

Pass an **`opts` bag** into composers (same style as your `calc*`):

```javascript
{
  localRatio: 0.55,
  cityRatio: 0.35,
  citySpillover: 0.2,
  parochialism: 25,
  crimeRelief: 1,
}
```

**Hardcode in the spec** (top of file): weights, breakpoints, “parochialism coefficient.”

**Pass at runtime**: district ratios, city aggregates, card stacks.

That way tuning is “edit `PUBLIC_ORDER_COMPOSE_WEIGHTS`” not “hunt through calc.”

```javascript
var PUBLIC_ORDER_COMPOSE = {
    citySpillover: 0.2,
    parochialismPerPoint: 0.0005,
}
```

---

## Composers vs band classifiers

| | Composer | Band classifier |
|---|----------|-----------------|
| Output | continuous (0..1 or domain float) | discrete string |
| Inputs | often **many** | usually **one ratio** |
| Player-facing | rarely shown directly | qdisplay / “contested” |
| Tuning | breakpoints + weights | threshold cutoffs |

You *can* derive bands from composed severity:

```javascript
moraleBand: publicOrderMoraleBandFromSeverity(severity)
```

But then band boundaries must match the curve — fiddly. **Usually better:** bands from **local `R`**, composer only **scales** the magnitude inside the band:

```javascript
var row = MORALE_EFFECT[balance.moraleBand]
var magnitude = row.magnitude * (0.5 + 0.5 * balance.severity)
```

Bands stay stable; severity smooths month-to-month wobble.

---

## When you need a composer (checklist)

- More than one ratio (local + city).
- Qualities that aren’t ratios (parochialism, `crime_relief_*`, leverage).
- Same curve reused with different blends (police hears local, city stat hears aggregate).
- Temporary shocks that shouldn’t rewrite breakpoint tables.

Skip the composer when `severity = publicOrderSeverity(ratio)` is enough.

---

## Debugging tip

Log one line per district per month from the composer:

```text
Pitts: localR=0.58 cityR=0.41 severity=0.52 band=contested
```

If severity and band ever feel wrong, you’ll see whether the bug is **blend** (composer), **bucket** (band thresholds), or **effect** (apply table).

---

**Short definition:** a composer is a **named, testable function** that turns several normalized inputs into **one severity** (or one pressure scalar), so `calc*` stays assembly and `apply*` stays “band → number.” Start with one weighted average for city spillover; add layers only when playtests show you need them.

## Formal definition

A **composer** (in this simulation sense) is a **pure function** that maps a **finite tuple of normalized inputs** to a **single scalar output** in a fixed domain (typically \([0, 1]\) or a game-specific range), according to an explicit **composition policy** \(\mathcal{C}\):

\[
\text{composer}_k : \mathcal{X}_k \to \mathbb{R}, \quad
\text{severity} = \text{composer}_k(\mathbf{x})
\]

where:

- \(k\) names the **semantic quantity** being composed (e.g. public-order pressure, corp-asset threat, morale drift signal).
- \(\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)\) is a **context bundle** (ratios, qualities, modifiers) gathered by a `calc*` function.
- Each \(x_i\) is either already in-domain or passed through a **primitive curve** \(f_i\) first (e.g. \(f(\text{localRatio})\)).
- \(\mathcal{C}\) is **documented and stable**: weighted sum, max, clamped sum, product dampening, etc.
- The composer **does not** assign discrete bands, **does not** apply game state mutations, and **does not** encode narrative one-off events unless those events are passed in as explicit inputs.

**Contrast:**

| Construct | Role | Output |
|-----------|------|--------|
| **Primitive curve** \(f\) | One meaningful input → continuous value | e.g. severity from one ratio |
| **Band classifier** \(B\) | Continuous or ratio input → discrete label | `'contested'` |
| **Composer** \(\mathcal{C}\) | Several inputs → **one** combined scalar | e.g. blended severity |
| **Effect map** \(E\) | Band (+ optional scalar) → gameplay deltas | morale −1, crime 7 |

Pipeline:

\[
\mathbf{x} \xrightarrow{\text{calc*}} \mathbf{x} \xrightarrow{f_i} \text{normalized inputs} \xrightarrow{\mathcal{C}} \text{severity} \xrightarrow{B} \text{band} \xrightarrow{E} \text{effects}
\]

(Band may be computed from a **subset** of \(\mathbf{x}\), not necessarily from severity — that’s intentional.)

---

## Additional best practices (beyond what we already discussed)

### 1. **One composer, one meaning**

A composer must answer exactly one question, e.g. “How threatened do corp assets feel?” Not “How bad is everything?” If you can’t name it in one sentence, split it.

### 2. **Idempotency on missing inputs**

Define defaults for every field in \(\mathbf{x}\) inside the composer (or a single `normalizeComposeOpts` helper). Callers should not need to know which inputs are optional. Document: *“Omitted `cityRatio` → treated as 0 (no city drag).”*

### 3. **Monotonicity (when possible)**

State which inputs should **worsen** severity when increased. Reviewers and future-you can then catch bugs (`crime_relief` accidentally adding severity). You don’t need strict monotonicity everywhere, but document exceptions (e.g. “high parochialism slightly **reduces** composed severity via watch bonus”).

### 4. **Commensurability before blending**

Only weighted-average inputs that are already the **same kind** of thing (two severities, two pressures). Don’t average ratio `0.6` with parochialism `25` — convert parochialism to a 0..1 **nudge** first, then add or blend.

### 5. **Separate “structural” vs “shock” composition**

- **Structural composer**: slow signals (ratios, prosperity, spillover) — runs every month.
- **Shock layer**: blind eye, raid heat — applied **after** \(\mathcal{C}\) as `clamp01(severity + shockDelta)` or a separate flag that bypasses the composer entirely.

Keeps narrative events from polluting the steady-state formula.

### 6. **Bounded output always**

Every composer ends with `clamp01` (or clamp to your domain). Composers stack; unclamped sums drift to absurdity when you add modifiers later.

### 7. **Version the policy, not the function name**

When \(\mathcal{C}\) changes materially, bump a comment or constant: `PUBLIC_ORDER_COMPOSE_V1`. Saves are sensitive to continuous severity even if players only see bands.

### 8. **Don’t compose inside apply***

Apply reads **finished** `severity` (or ignores it). If apply recomposes, you get double-counting when the monthly tick also composes.

### 9. **Invertibility / debug mode (optional but valuable)**

For tuning, expose or log intermediate terms:

```text
severity = 0.52 = local(0.58)×0.8 + city(0.35)×0.2 − relief(0.02)
```

Composers that return `{ value, terms: { local, city, relief } }` in dev builds make balance work much less fiddly.

### 10. **Prefer associative building blocks**

Implement \(\mathcal{C}\) from a small library:

- `mix(a, b, weight)` — weighted average  
- `boost(base, delta)` — clamped add  
- `dampen(base, factor)` — multiply in \([0,1]\)  
- `worstOf(a, b)` — max  

New composers become **recipes**, not new math each time.

### 11. **Order sensitivity: document it**

`boost(mix(a,b), c)` ≠ `mix(boost(a,c), boost(b,c))` in general. Write one canonical order in the design doc: e.g. *“blend local/city first, then subtract relief, then clamp.”*

### 12. **Composers are not aggregators across entities**

Composing **per district**, then averaging districts, ≠ composing **citywide inputs** once. Decide:

- city `parochialism` → one city composer input, or  
- district severities → weighted mean **after** per-district composers.

Mixing the two levels is a common source of “why is Deeps weird?”

### 13. **Test at boundaries**

For each composer, pin cases:

| Case | Expect |
|------|--------|
| All inputs neutral / zero | severity at defined baseline (often 0) |
| One input at max, others min | severity moves in documented direction |
| Missing optional inputs | same as neutral defaults |
| Both inputs max | clamped, not > 1 |

### 14. **When not to use a composer**

Use a primitive curve only when there is literally one driver. Use a **direct override** when a cable event says “LE discounted 50%” — pass `leDiscount: 0.5` into calc, not a composer that tries to infer it from other stats.

---

## Compact formal summary

> A **composer** is a pure, named composition policy \(\mathcal{C}_k\) that fuses multiple normalized simulation inputs into a single scalar severity for quantity \(k\), with bounded output and explicit defaults, sitting between input assembly (`calc*`) and discrete effect application (`apply*`), and distinct from both primitive curves (one input) and band classifiers (discrete labels).

That’s the whole idea in one sentence for docs; everything else is discipline so the scalar stays meaningful as you add syndicates, spillover, and event shocks.

## [2026-06-08T13:34:08Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

Your intuition is solid. What you’ve been calling **“mappable functions”** usually shows up in the wild under several names, depending on which part of the pipeline you’re looking at.

## Closest established terms

| What you’re doing | Common names | Where you’ll see it |
|-------------------|--------------|---------------------|
| One input → one output via a curve/table | **Response function**, **transfer function**, **mapping**, **lookup table (LUT)** | Games (`Smoothstep`, `FInterp`), audio, control theory |
| Several inputs → one scalar | **Aggregator**, **reducer**, **mixer**, **blend function**, **scoring function** | FP, analytics, game AI |
| The whole calc → curve → combine → effect chain | **Pipeline**, **dataflow**, **signal chain** | Unix pipes, graphics compositors, audio DAWs |
| Swappable “how we combine” logic | **Strategy** (policy object) | Gang of Four |
| Small tweak wrapped around a base value | **Decorator** (or **modifier layer**) | OOP patterns, RPG “stat modifiers” |

**Composer** isn’t a Gang-of-Four pattern name, but it’s the same *role* as an **aggregator with a documented composition policy** — or, in game dev docs, a **derived stat formula**.

Your “mappable function” is often literally a **remap**: domain value → codomain value, sometimes piecewise (breakpoints) or smooth (ease curves).

---

## Patterns that are basically “composer ecosystems”

### 1. **Pipeline / signal chain**

Stages with one direction of flow:

```text
raw → normalize → curve → compose → classify → apply
```

Audio and graphics people say **signal chain**; backend people say **pipeline**. Same shape.

### 2. **Normalize → weigh → combine** (aggregator recipe)

Very common in:

- Search ranking (**scoring functions**)
- ML (**feature fusion**)
- Dashboards (**composite KPIs**)
- RPGs (**derived attributes**: `AC = base + dexMod + armorMod`)

The composer is the **combine** step; curves are **per-feature normalization**.

### 3. **Separation: classifier vs regressor**

ML vocabulary maps cleanly to your split:

- **Classifier** → band (`contested`)
- **Regressor** → continuous severity (`0.76`)

Game designers often keep both: label for UI, float for tuning.

### 4. **Layered composition (structural + shock)**

Sometimes called:

- **Base + modifier** (CRPG stats)
- **Two-phase evaluation** (steady state, then overrides)
- **Decorator chain** (each layer wraps the previous)

Your “shock events bypass the composer” is **override semantics**, not composition — also a named idea.

### 5. **Policy / strategy object**

When \(\mathcal{C}\) might change (e.g. ceasefire changes how city spillover works), the pattern is **Strategy**: same `compose(opts)`, different policy implementation or config table.

### 6. **Table-driven design**

Breakpoints in data instead of `switch` — **data-oriented** or **lookup-driven** logic. Common in games because designers edit tables.

---

## Functional programming vocabulary (useful, not mandatory)

- **Function composition** \( (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) \) — chaining curves.
- **Reducer / fold** — many inputs → one output (`mix`, `max`, `sum` with clamp).
- **Monoid** — if your combine is associative and has an identity (weighted average with fixed weights is a nice mental model).

You don’t need the math words to use the ideas; they explain why **order of operations** and **defaults** matter.

---

## Game-dev terms you’ll recognize

- **Remap / MapRange** — linear or curved remap between intervals  
- **Curve asset / response curve** — designer-authored \(f\)  
- **Derived stat** — anything produced by a composer-like formula  
- **Attribute stack** — base + modifiers (composer + decorators)

Unreal’s **Float Curve** assets are primitive curves; your composer is what blends several curve outputs.

---

## What to call it in *your* docs

For Mikasa / crime QNM, I’d use:

- **Curve** — one meaningful input → float (`publicOrderSeverity`)
- **Composer** — several normalized inputs → one float (`composePublicOrderSeverity`)
- **Classifier** — float/ratio → band (`publicOrderMoraleBand`)
- **Effect table** — band → gameplay delta (`applyPublicOrderMoraleEffects`)

That’s precise enough for future you and doesn’t fight existing literature.

---

## One sentence tie-in to your history

You’ve been building **pipelines of remappable functions** with occasional **aggregators** at the end; naming the aggregator a **composer** and forcing **one semantic question per composer** is the missing bit that stops “mappable functions” from turning into one giant unmappable knot.

If you want reading that matches this without formal CS depth: look up **“response curves game design”**, **“derived stats RPG”**, and **“feature normalization”** in scoring/ranking posts — same bones, different skins.
